newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says to discuss liberalising insurance fees.
newsitem.headline: Japan says to discuss liberalising insurance fees.

text.p: Japan will explain to the United States its plans to liberalise market commission fees, including those for insurance, during bilateral insurance talks on Friday, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said.
"I think they will wish us success with our 'Big Bang' market reforms," Mitsuzuka told a news conference.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto unveiled plans on Monday to liberalise Japan's financial markets over the next five years and to catch up with reforms carried out more than a decade ago in Europe and North America.
Japan and the United States are set to hold working-level talks concerning their dispute on how to go about deregulating Japan's insurance market on November 15 and 16 in San Francisco.

Mitsuzuka said he has instructed MOF officials attending the talks to work towards meeting the agreed deadline of December 15. Japan will further explain its position on the talks and ask the U.S. side for understanding, he added.

The finance minister plans to call in various government panels associated with the financial deregulation to the ministry at 2.45 p.m. (0545 GMT) to explain Hashimoto's plans and urge speedy deliberations.
Mitsuzuka said the ministry was working towards setting up a meeting with U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan when he visits Japan from Nov 17 to Nov 19, but no dates have been set.

Asked about an agreement reached with two other parties to hive off the ministry's inspection function of the banking industry into a separate body, Mitsuzuka said he would respect the agreement. Mitsuzuka said he will meet with senior officials from the Social Democratic Party and Sakigake Party later today to discuss MOF's reforms.
